# Historical branches — Symbol, Account and Trust

This authored companion develops independently checked branches beside the protected [HISTORY](HISTORY.md). It does not replace that encounter or promote all its leads to evidence. Its lexical findings **historicise** the [whole field](WHOLE-FIELD.md); their operational consequences return there under separately declared registers. Sources below were consulted on 8 September 2026. Dictionary evidence establishes the indicated forms and senses; a dictionary's cited ancient passages are locators until read independently.

## Matching tokens and institutional recognition

**Register 2 — attested semantic field.** LSJ, s.v. **σύμβολον**, I.1, records a token consisting of corresponding pieces retained by parties for subsequent recognition. It cites Herodotus 6.86, Euripides *Medea* 613 and Plato *Symposium* 191d among its witnesses. I.3 records guarantee; I.5 records civic tokens through which entitlement and payment were administered. These entries establish differentiated uses, rather than a single abstract definition applicable to every occurrence. [LSJ, Scaife ATLAS](../../sources/classical-philology/liddell-scott-jones/lsj-1940-greek-english-lexicon/lsj-1940-greek-english-lexicon.md#lsj-1940-greek-english-lexicon-q010).

The physical seam makes correspondence inspectable. The history therefore supplies a determinate operation for the whole field: a present object directs recognition toward a counterpart and an acknowledged relation. The essay's further requirement that symbolic efficacy remain answerable to source is **register 3**, argued from this material witness and the native symbolic relation. An authentic token does not by itself establish the justice of the obligation or guarantee a bearer's future conduct.

**Remaining primary task:** collate Herodotus 6.86's deposit and token narrative, *Medea* 608–615's offer and response, and the philosophical transformation at *Symposium* 191d in their distinct contexts before making passage-level claims about them. The dictionary has been read; those three primary tellings have not been newly read in this development. Greek συμβάλλω/διαβάλλω morphology and the chronological development of accusation retain their separate lexical task in the two-logics history. The present acquisition supports the matching-token sense without pretending to complete that history.

The [zero–subject development](../../histories/traditions-and-disciplines/zero-subject-advent/DEVELOPMENT.md) **historicises** the authorial braid of two admissions. A sign acquires arithmetic powers; a represented psychic or perspectival condition acquires an investigative office. Symbol answers to source at register 3 by preserving each achievement and its distinct history. Integral return does not turn every earlier token into the final Symbol.

## Reckoning, report and a split debt record

**Registers 1 and 2, separately.** English *account* is traced through Middle English and Anglo-French forms associated with counting. Its attested senses include transaction records, explanations and narrative reports. This supports the relation between reckoning and telling without making every act of narration financial. The entry does not warrant promoting the protected HISTORY's “cut together” gloss to the public etymology of *account*. [Merriam-Webster, “account,” Word History and senses 1–3](../../sources/language-literary-studies/merriam-webster/merriam-webster-online-dictionary/merriam-webster-online-dictionary.md#merriam-webster-online-dictionary-q006).

**Material historical witness.** The Bank of England Museum's wooden tally **A013/1** records one of the Bank's first loans to the Government in **1694**. The notched hazelwood was split lengthwise, leaving each party a record of the debt. Its material division and shared reckoning supply an independently documented historical comparison with the Greek token. No borrowing route between the two institutions has been established here. [Bank of England Museum, “Payments through time,” Wooden tally stick](../../sources/political-theory-institutions/bank-of-england/bank-of-england-2019-payments-through-time/bank-of-england-2019-payments-through-time.md#bank-of-england-2019-payments-through-time-q001).

The comparison returns to [Account's source relation](WHOLE-FIELD.md#account-does-not-replace-source) at register 3. A record can preserve the amount and identify an obligation while depending on persons, institutions and resources for its discharge. Matching records support the account's integrity; payment and the conditions of repayment are further events. The particular tally's museum record is not evidence for a universal history of money, a complete account of Exchequer procedure or the moral legitimacy of a debt.

The protected branches on *computare*, *reckon*, *rule*, *right*, *credit*, *record*, *coin*, *claim*, *fiat*, *value*, *score* and *digit* retain their individual source tasks. Especially, reconstructed heart/credit relations and the legal history of circulating claims require their own witnesses. This companion does not infer common descent from a shared operation of keeping account.

The [language, symbol and dialogue development](../../histories/traditions-and-disciplines/language-symbol-dialogue/DEVELOPMENT.md) **historicises** the passage from an articulated sign to the practices through which it is used and answered. Reference, rule-following, situated address and suspended assumption retain different carriers. At register 3, the received account owes those conditions to its next use rather than treating a shared word for language as their common source.

The [Baudrillard lens](../../sources/media-technology-philosophy/baudrillard/baudrillard-1976-symbolic-exchange-death/baudrillard-1976-symbolic-exchange-death.md#baudrillard-lens-reading) **qualifies** the record/source distinction at register 3 by asking how an account helps produce what it then describes. The three historical orders and four image phases keep different purposes; the symbolic’s reversibility does not promise benign reconciliation. The analysis itself must remain capable of receiving a source correction.

## Reliance and entrusted office

**Register 1 — bounded lexical claim.** Merriam-Webster gives Middle English *trust* a **probably Scandinavian** origin, relating it to Old Norse *traust* and Old English *trēowe*. The uncertainty belongs to that transmission claim and remains explicit. **Register 2:** the entry distinguishes reliance, contingent hope, custody or responsible office, and credit for future payment. Those senses locate several historical-language offices without identifying them all with the essay's formal-limit argument. [Merriam-Webster, “trust,” senses 1, 4–5 and Word History](../../sources/language-literary-studies/merriam-webster/merriam-webster-online-dictionary/merriam-webster-online-dictionary.md#merriam-webster-online-dictionary-q007).

The [Trust operation](WHOLE-FIELD.md#trust-keeps-the-return-route-active) draws a further **register-3** distinction: someone can know the stated obligation and still have to commit to a relation in which its fulfilment remains consequential. The public dictionary does not derive knowledge's dependence on trust, prove a theological doctrine of faith or prescribe the essay's covenant architecture. Those operations have their own authorial and argument carriers. Fides/credere, covenant traditions and comparative institutional histories remain in their existing homes.

The [formal-limit dossier](../../dossiers/formal-limit.md#e3-e4-consumer-return) **qualifies** the Trust branch through separate consequences of formation, derivability, elucidation and predication. Their conditions remain available for inquiry. The further undertaking of using an examined account belongs to register 3 and cannot be manufactured by a shared word for limit.

<a id="reference-38-hal-and-hole"></a>
## Reference 38 — hāl, whole, holy, health; the separate hole

The [reference-38 note](../../../../section-rooms/arguments/concepts/reference-notes/hole-whole-holy-health.md) distinguished lexical kinship from poetic crossing, but its historical destination lacked the branch. This section supplies that missing destination, with the following independently consulted lexical inputs.

| Term | Bounded historical finding | Evidence register and witness |
| --- | --- | --- |
| *whole* | Middle English *hool* continues Old English *hāl*, associated with soundness, freedom from injury and entirety. | 1; [Merriam-Webster, “whole,” Word History](../../sources/language-literary-studies/merriam-webster/merriam-webster-online-dictionary/merriam-webster-online-dictionary.md#merriam-webster-online-dictionary-q008) |
| *holy* | The entry traces the word to Old English *hālig* and states kinship with *hāl*. Its wording “akin” is not represented here as a complete derivational demonstration. | 1; [Merriam-Webster, “holy,” Word History](../../sources/language-literary-studies/merriam-webster/merriam-webster-online-dictionary/merriam-webster-online-dictionary.md#merriam-webster-online-dictionary-q009) |
| *health* | Middle English *helthe* continues Old English *hǣlth*, derived from *hāl*. | 1; [Merriam-Webster, “health,” Word History](../../sources/language-literary-studies/merriam-webster/merriam-webster-online-dictionary/merriam-webster-online-dictionary.md#merriam-webster-online-dictionary-q010) |
| *heal* | Middle English *helen* continues Old English *hǣlan*; the entry relates it to *hāl*. | 1; [Merriam-Webster, “heal,” Word History](../../sources/language-literary-studies/merriam-webster/merriam-webster-online-dictionary/merriam-webster-online-dictionary.md#merriam-webster-online-dictionary-q011) |
| *hole* | Middle English *hole/holle* continues Old English *hol*, the hollow-place noun associated with the adjective for hollowness. This is a separate historical line from *hāl*. | 1; [Merriam-Webster, “hole,” Word History](../../sources/language-literary-studies/merriam-webster/merriam-webster-online-dictionary/merriam-webster-online-dictionary.md#merriam-webster-online-dictionary-q012) |

At **register 2**, soundness and intactness provide a historical semantic field for thinking about wholeness. They do not establish a historical doctrine that integrity requires sealing every opening. Sacredness likewise cannot be reduced to bodily health on the strength of kinship among words. The specific attested senses and later institutions must retain their differences.

At **register 4**, the English sound-match between *hole* and *whole* permits the authorial chiasm already retained in the reference note: “The hole is the false cognate that tells the structural truth: some wholes remain whole only by keeping their opening open.” This is poetic re-entry after the lexical distinction has been made. It does not repair a missing etymological connection; its force depends on allowing the two histories to remain separate.

At **register 3**, the field gives the crossing an exact epistemic consequence. An account preserves its integrity through an opening by which source, reply and consequence can alter it. Closing that route can preserve the wording while destroying its fidelity. The conceptual return goes through [A20's image/source relation](../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A20-Image-Valuation-Possession.md), [C27's protected criterion](../../../../section-rooms/arguments/concepts/C27-Protected-Account-Occupied-Zero-Source-Claim.md) and [A32's changed future field](../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A32-Reflective-Field-The-Mirror-That-Moves-First.md), then back to [the whole field's return](WHOLE-FIELD.md#opening-and-integrity). No new consumer edge is claimed to have been installed by this historical development.

The toroidal image remains available in the native formal work, but no topological theorem follows from English homophony. A future figure must distinguish the lexicon's two descent lines from the dashed poetic crossing and from any separately warranted topological object. Reference 38 is historically placed here; a universal genealogy of holiness or a clinical account of health is not thereby completed.

The [Indian philosophy dossier](../../dossiers/indian-philosophy.md#50--the-next-act-must-inherit-the-return) **extends** the source-distinct Indian comparison into the full functional return cycle; E4’s four operations retain their distinct burdens.

## Branches kept in their own soils

The protected HISTORY retains five independent comparisons: Sanskrit enumeration, Hebrew counting/writing, Chinese rectification of names, Arabic reckoning and Egyptian naming. Each has its own lexical and textual or material practice. They supply no hidden roots for the three English terms and introduce no new E4 primitives. The developed cases below return through the four existing operations, retaining which practice is textually prescribed, which object survives, and which consequence belongs to the essay.


<a id="sanskrit-enumeration-and-discriminative-practice"></a>
### Sanskrit enumeration and discriminative practice

**Evidence register 2:** the Sanskrit lexical entries and the selected Sāṃkhyakārikā passages. **Register 3:** their expressly authored return through Symbol / Account / Trust. This case develops the Sanskrit lead beside the protected HISTORY; its historical standing does not supply or diminish the native field’s force.

[Monier-Williams’s saṃ-√khyā and saṃkhyā entries](../../sources/classical-philology/monier-williams/monier-williams-1899-sanskrit-english-dictionary/monier-williams-1899-sanskrit-english-dictionary.md#monier-williams-1899-sanskrit-english-dictionary-p001) distinguish counting up, a number or total, grammatical number, deliberation and an appellation. The related [sāṃkhya entry](../../sources/classical-philology/monier-williams/monier-williams-1899-sanskrit-english-dictionary/monier-williams-1899-sanskrit-english-dictionary.md#monier-williams-1899-sanskrit-english-dictionary-p002) gives numerical and discriminative uses and the philosophical school’s name. It retains two explanations of that name: discrimination and, in the lexicographer’s qualified preference, enumeration of twenty-five principles. This lexical evidence establishes a Sanskrit field of uses. The philosophy’s operation has to be recovered from its own text.

Īśvarakṛṣṇa’s classical formulation is conventionally placed around 350 CE, with the author’s precise date uncertain. The selected primary-language carrier is Ruzsa’s dated 1998 electronic recension, whose header identifies its print sources and variants; the existing 1837 Colebrooke/Wilson translation remains a distinct witness. [Kārikā 3](../../sources/indian-philosophy/isvarakrishna/isvarakrishna-ruzsa-1998-samkhyakarika/isvarakrishna-ruzsa-1998-samkhyakarika.md#isvarakrishna-ruzsa-1998-samkhyakarika-p001) divides the principles by what produces and what is produced. Root prakṛti is not itself a product. Seven principles beginning with mahat are both produced and productive; sixteen are products; puruṣa is neither. The enumeration therefore retains four causal descriptions within its total of twenty-five.

The seven comprise buddhi, ahaṃkāra and five subtle elements. The sixteen comprise the eleven faculties, including manas, and the five gross elements. A count which replaced these relations with twenty-five interchangeable units would lose what the classification explains. Nor does placing puruṣa twenty-fifth mean that only one person exists: verse 18 separately argues for a plurality of puruṣas. Enumeration makes the principles addressable while their causal and cognitive offices remain different. It supplies no equation with Trika’s thirty-six tattvas or Taylor’s eight determinations.

The text then asks how those principles are known. [Kārikās 4–6](../../sources/indian-philosophy/isvarakrishna/isvarakrishna-ruzsa-1998-samkhyakarika/isvarakrishna-ruzsa-1998-samkhyakarika.md#isvarakrishna-ruzsa-1998-samkhyakarika-p002) distinguish perception, inference and trustworthy testimony. Perceptual determination has its objects; inference works through a sign and what it indicates; reliable testimony has a further office where the other means do not establish the matter. Listing the principles and warranting knowledge of them are thus consecutive, distinguishable acts. The source’s admitted testimony is a particular epistemic means. Taylor’s Trust is the broader committed relation within which an examined account can enter action; neither term silently acquires the other’s whole scope.

The enumeration also belongs to a practice. In [Kārikās 64–68](../../sources/indian-philosophy/isvarakrishna/isvarakrishna-ruzsa-1998-samkhyakarika/isvarakrishna-ruzsa-1998-samkhyakarika.md#isvarakrishna-ruzsa-1998-samkhyakarika-p003), repeated discrimination of the principles releases the appropriation of activity and possession to puruṣa. The distinction changes the practitioner’s relation to experience. The continuation of the body through prior dispositions, figured by a turning wheel, is distinguished from final isolation at bodily dissolution. The passage’s direction is Sāṃkhya liberation through discrimination. E4’s continuing return through changed encounters is a separately authored operation; it does not turn the inactive puruṣa into an agent of mutual revision.

At **register 3**, **Symbol answers to source** when a named principle retains the relation which lets it be recognised here. **Account does not replace source** when the enumeration carries both its classification criterion and the means by which the claim is known. **Trust keeps the return route active** in the authorial comparison when reliance on a teaching retains access to its warrant and use; the historical testimony passage alone does not demonstrate that every teaching permits correction. **Account re-enters source-field** when the practised discrimination changes subsequent appropriation. The last relation compares a specified transformation while preserving the difference between Sāṃkhya’s isolating release and E4’s recursive source-answerability.

This case returns a precise burden to [A15](../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A15-Ratio-Rationality-Measure-Reckoning-Harmony-Account.md): an exact count must retain the criterion which made its members countable. It also returns to [C10](../../../../section-rooms/arguments/concepts/C10-Mediation-Pramana.md): an acquired statement retains whether its warrant was perception, inference or reliable testimony. The comparison develops E4’s three terms and four operations through a specific philosophical practice, without treating lexical kinship as proof of the system’s ontology or asserting transmission to another language.

**Remaining source scope:** Print collation of Cologne dictionary transcription and GRETIL constituent editions; exact quotation readiness is not claimed. Precise ancient composition date; no comprehensive history of the name or all Sāṃkhya practices admitted.


<a id="hebrew-spr-counting-writing-and-entrusted-work"></a>
### Hebrew SPR: counting, writing and entrusted work

**Evidence register 2:** the separate Hebrew lexical entries and selected biblical passages. **Register 3:** the authorial comparison through Symbol / Account / Trust. SPR names a Hebrew lexical field here; it is neither a proposed ancestor of the English terms nor a name for their native relation.

[Brown–Driver–Briggs distinguishes](../../sources/biblical-studies/brown-driver-briggs/bdb-hebrew-english-lexicon-online/bdb-hebrew-english-lexicon-online.md#bdb-hebrew-english-lexicon-online-p001) counting under Qal sāfar from recounting under Piʿel, while also recording precise counting in the latter stem. The sōfēr subentry differentiates an enumerator, muster-officer, secretary and scribe. [Sēfer](../../sources/biblical-studies/brown-driver-briggs/bdb-hebrew-english-lexicon-online/bdb-hebrew-english-lexicon-online.md#bdb-hebrew-english-lexicon-online-p002) includes missive, legal document, book or scroll, and writing or book-learning. [Mispār](../../sources/biblical-studies/brown-driver-briggs/bdb-hebrew-english-lexicon-online/bdb-hebrew-english-lexicon-online.md#bdb-hebrew-english-lexicon-online-p003) includes number and a separately attested recounting sense. These are related forms with differentiated offices. The lexicon’s probable derivation of sāfar from sēfer, and its probable Assyrian explanation of sēfer, remain qualified historical proposals. A confident story in which one primordial tally generates all writing would exceed the admitted evidence.

The primary carrier is Mechon Mamre’s Hebrew text with English based on JPS 1917. Its edition date is distinct from the chronology narrated within Kings and from the unresolved dating of textual composition. [Genesis 15:1–6](../../sources/biblical-studies/anonymous/hebrew-bible-mechon-mamre-jps1917/hebrew-bible-mechon-mamre-jps1917.md#hebrew-bible-mechon-mamre-jps1917-p001) places counting the stars within Abram’s question about an heir and a promise in which he comes to believe. The SPR forms perform the count. Believing belongs to ʾMN; the reckoning in the next clause belongs to ḤŠB. Their encounter in one passage therefore gives count, reliance and reckoning a textual relation without inventing lexical identity among them.

A public account receives a different consequence in [2 Kings 8:1–6](../../sources/biblical-studies/anonymous/hebrew-bible-mechon-mamre-jps1917/hebrew-bible-mechon-mamre-jps1917.md#hebrew-bible-mechon-mamre-jps1917-p002). A woman returns after seven years away during famine and petitions for her house and land. The king has asked Gehazi to recount Elisha’s deeds; while he tells the story of her son, she appears. Gehazi identifies her, but the king also asks her directly, and she gives her account. He then commissions an officer to restore her possessions and the field’s produce since her departure. SPR forms mark both the prior telling and her answer. Her account confirms the narrative here; the text does not report her correcting Gehazi. What changes is its office: a remembered deed enters a current claim upon property and a consequential order. The passage records that order, not an independently verified execution of it.

[The repair narrative in 2 Kings 12:5–17](../../sources/biblical-studies/anonymous/hebrew-bible-mechon-mamre-jps1917/hebrew-bible-mechon-mamre-jps1917.md#hebrew-bible-mechon-mamre-jps1917-p003) supplies a dated practice within its own chronology. In Jehoash’s twenty-third regnal year, the building remains unrepaired. The king challenges the failed arrangement; a chest receives the money; the royal scribe and high priest count it; funds go to workers and materials. The count serves a material purpose whose failure had already prompted a change of arrangements. Yet 12:16 says that no reckoning was made with the entrusted men because they dealt faithfully. The SPR term here names the scribe; the counting verb is MNH, the reckoning verb ḤŠB and faithfulness ʾMN. The narrative differentiates recorded resources, their actual use and confidence in persons. It resists treating more accounting as a sufficient cause of trust.

The same relation acquires a written authority in [2 Kings 22:3–20](../../sources/biblical-studies/anonymous/hebrew-bible-mechon-mamre-jps1917/hebrew-bible-mechon-mamre-jps1917.md#hebrew-bible-mechon-mamre-jps1917-p004), placed in Josiah’s eighteenth year. Shaphan the scribe is sent about repair funds. Hilkiah gives him the found law-book; Shaphan reads it and then reads it before the king. Hearing it changes the king’s response into mourning and a commission to inquire, which leads to Huldah. The book and scribe are SPR forms; the acts of reading and reporting use other roots. The source presents a sequence of entrusted offices and consequential reception. It does not settle the found book’s composition date or authenticate an unrestricted contemporary claim to speak in its name.

At **register 3**, **Symbol answers to source** when the scribe, text or teller retains the particular relation it claims to bear. **Account does not replace source** when counted money remains distinguishable from repaired fabric, and a narrated person can still answer the hearer directly. **Trust keeps the return route active** as an authorial requirement: an undertaking sustains use while leaving consequences and affected persons able to reach the commission. The biblical praise of faithful work does not itself prescribe that whole requirement. **Account re-enters source-field** has a concrete comparison in the altered repair arrangement and in a telling which becomes a restoration order. The narrated action and the further norm of revisability retain separate standing.

The return to [A15](../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A15-Ratio-Rationality-Measure-Reckoning-Harmony-Account.md) distinguishes resource, record and criterion; the return to [A33](../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A33-Epistemic-Cultivation-Operational-Parity.md) asks what the received account changed. Inspectable evidence could establish a restoration order while leaving its execution unproved. Keeping that difference changes the next permissible claim. These Hebrew cases therefore deepen E4 through their particular practices while leaving Sanskrit enumeration, Greek tokens and later English accounting in their distinct histories.

**Remaining source scope:** BDB print/typesetting collation; proposed earlier derivations remain qualified. Absolute event/composition dating and historical execution of narrated commissions; no archaeological verification claimed.

<a id="chinese-rectification-of-names"></a>
### Chinese rectification of names — speech must sustain its office

*Zhèngmíng* supplies a political case in which a name must sustain the action it authorises. The [Ministry of Education dictionary](../../sources/classical-philology/ministry-of-education-taiwan/moe-2021-revised-mandarin-dictionary/moe-2021-revised-mandarin-dictionary.md#moe-2021-revised-mandarin-dictionary-q001) **sources** the lexical case: it records the correction of names toward correspondence with actuality and cites Analects 13.3. Its separate sense concerning substantive office is a further lexical use, not the hidden meaning of that passage. This is an independently witnessed Chinese semantic field; it contributes no ancestry for English Symbol, Account or Trust.

In the [received exchange, Analects 13.3](../../sources/chinese-philosophy/confucius/analects-ctext-legge/analects-ctext-legge.md#analects-ctext-legge-q001), Zilu asks what should come first if the Master governs Wei. Rectification initially appears to him remote from practical affairs. The answer makes that apparent remoteness consequential: names condition speech, speech the conduct of affairs, affairs the flourishing of rites and music, and these the fitting administration of punishment. The final exposure falls upon people who can no longer orient their actions. The opening restraint concerning what one does not know and the closing demand that speech be practicable belong to the same argument. A name has not answered merely because an authority has pronounced it. This is the received text's normative political sequence; its representation of government does not establish that the sequence was implemented or empirically verified.

E4's authorial comparison follows the office of the account through this sequence. **Symbol answers to source:** the designation must retain a relation to the conduct or role it presents. **Account does not replace source:** an orderly description of office cannot alone perform its obligations, and the consequences of its administration remain part of what the description must answer for. These operations preserve the political specificity of the source. They do not turn 名 into a word for every token, model or ledger, nor turn the passage into a QL derivation.

**Trust keeps the return route active** adds E4's own requirement: people who must act under a designation need more than a legible command. The relation between declared office, practicable speech and its consequences must remain answerable. [Analects 13.15](../../sources/chinese-philosophy/confucius/analects-ctext-legge/analects-ctext-legge.md#analects-ctext-legge-q002) **qualifies** the return with a particular comparison at this point. The pleasure of never being contradicted becomes dangerous where the ruler's words are bad; the passage distinguishes that case from unopposed good counsel and resists the claim that a single sentence mechanically makes or ruins a state. It supplies neither a modern right of dissent nor proof that every stable standard is protected. The comparison locates a failure precisely where an office's speech can no longer meet the correction its consequences require.

**Account re-enters source-field:** in E4, the return must be able to reach the authority and criterion sustaining the name, rather than blaming every failure upon those named. This final operation is Taylor's Argued development. The received political text makes the cost of naming concrete and supplies a warning about unopposed bad counsel; the requirement for an effective route of revision keeps its own authorial standing. Trust here names E4's enacted relation, not a Chinese lexical translation supplied by 13.3.


The comparison **returns-to** [Account’s source relation](WHOLE-FIELD.md#account-does-not-replace-source) through [A15](../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A15-Ratio-Rationality-Measure-Reckoning-Harmony-Account.md): the measure must retain the office and obligations it judges. It **returns-to** [Trust’s continuing route](WHOLE-FIELD.md#trust-keeps-the-return-route-active) through [C27](../../../../section-rooms/arguments/concepts/C27-Protected-Account-Occupied-Zero-Source-Claim.md): warranted stable counsel remains distinct from an office immune to correction. These are authorial consequences for the existing consumers. Critical manuscript collation, a selected Legge print edition, a specific Wei succession dispute and historical implementation or reception remain Open.


<a id="arabic-reckoning-and-names"></a>
### Arabic reckoning and the Names — an account, an address and an undertaking

Arabic supplies several related offices, with their words and textual occasions distinguished. [Lane’s ḥisāb entry](../../sources/classical-philology/lane/lane-arabic-english-lexicon-online/lane-arabic-english-lexicon-online.md#lane-arabic-english-lexicon-online-p001) and [separate aḥṣā entry](../../sources/classical-philology/lane/lane-arabic-english-lexicon-online/lane-arabic-english-lexicon-online.md#lane-arabic-english-lexicon-online-p002) **historicise** *ḥisāb* as reckoning and the separate form-IV *aḥṣā* through enumeration, registration, memory and knowledge. The two are not one root. A shared English gloss for counting cannot decide what either does in a particular passage.

The [Qur’anic sequence, 17:12–15](../../sources/religion-theology/quran/quran-arberry-corpus-selected/quran-arberry-corpus-selected.md#quran-arberry-corpus-selected-p001) **sources** a movement from the signs by which years become reckonable to the book a person confronts at resurrection. The bearer must read; accountability returns to the life whose record is presented. The adjacent verse preserves individual responsibility. In the selected Arberry rendering, this is a divine judgment scene. E4 receives the record’s demand for answerability without recasting divine judgment as an institutional ledger whose criterion the judged person can revise. The account and the life are placed in relation; their relation is the scene’s work.

[Qur’an 7:180](../../sources/religion-theology/quran/quran-arberry-corpus-selected/quran-arberry-corpus-selected.md#quran-arberry-corpus-selected-p002) **sources** a different act: calling upon God through the Names. Its wording does not give their number. [Al-Bukhārī 7392](../../sources/religion-theology/al-bukhari/bukhari-sahih-sunnah-online/bukhari-sahih-sunnah-online.md#bukhari-sahih-sunnah-online-p001), in a ninth-century collection whose compiler died in 870 CE, **sources** the separate ninety-nine-Names report. The displayed Muhsin Khan translation interprets *aḥṣāhā* through memorisation. That interpretive choice is preserved beside the Arabic verb’s broader lexical range. Neither this report nor the Qur’anic verse supplies a complete list or a bead-recitation protocol. Their recovered practice is textual invocation and the undertaking associated with enumeration or retention, not an independently observed performance of a later devotional order.

The sequence returns to [the whole field](WHOLE-FIELD.md) at register 3. **Symbol answers to source:** a Name functions as address within a tradition of attribution, not as the interpreter’s possession of what is addressed. **Account does not replace source:** the count organises a finite undertaking while neither the numeral nor a translation exhausts its religious object. **Trust keeps the return route active:** the reported promise gives memorisation or enumeration an orientation toward fulfilment; E4’s further duty of answerability belongs to the essay and must not be silently attributed to the hadith. **Account re-enters source-field:** the retained wording can shape a subsequent act of invocation and a reader’s account of responsibility. This is the proposed operational consequence of using the text, not a reported psychological experiment or evidence that a promised afterlife outcome occurred.

This branch changes the comparison by refusing to let count stand for the whole event. It makes the object counted, the act performed, the attribution and the promised consequence separately available. Its Qur’anic, hadith and nineteenth-century lexicographic witnesses retain their own times and textual offices. No descent into the English words Symbol, Account or Trust, and no identity with the Egyptian name-preserving practice, follows.

The case **returns-to** [A15](../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A15-Ratio-Rationality-Measure-Reckoning-Harmony-Account.md) with the counted object, textual warrant and further act specified; it **returns-to** [A23](../../../../section-rooms/arguments/A23-Trust-Faith-and-the-Formal-Limit.md) with the undertaking distinguished from empirical verification of its promised outcome. Their native arguments are not derived from the numerical formula. Complete Names lists, particular recitation technologies and the historical dating of the individual Qur’anic verses remain outside this acquired scope.

<a id="egyptian-rn-reri"></a>
### Egyptian rn — the name retained for a particular deceased person

The [TLA rn entry, lemma 94700](../../sources/classical-philology/tla/tla-hieroglyphic-hieratic-lexicon/tla-hieroglyphic-hieratic-lexicon.md#tla-hieroglyphic-hieratic-lexicon-p001) **historicises** the hieroglyphic/hieratic noun for name. This lexical identity establishes the point of departure; the further claim about continued personhood needs a particular practice. The entry’s corpus-wide attestation span is not a date for every use, and its separate Demotic relations do not erase changes of language and period.

[Reri’s funerary papyrus, British Museum EA75044,4](../../sources/religion-theology/reri/reri-ptolemaic-funerary-papyrus/reri-ptolemaic-funerary-papyrus.md#reri-ptolemaic-funerary-papyrus-p001) **sources** such a practice in Ptolemaic Thebes. The museum’s period range is 305–30 BCE; it is not an exact production year. In its hieratic Book of the Dead arrangement, spell 25 occupies the top of column 3 and concerns remembrance of the deceased’s name. Its neighbours restore speech and protect the heart. The name thus appears within a programme for the continued capacities of this deceased person, rather than as an isolated entry in a universal inventory of soul-parts.

The medium performs a prospective act. A surviving written arrangement supplies what the ritual anticipates the deceased needing beyond death. Its intended result is preservation of named continuity; the papyrus’s existence and the museum’s identification establish that this provision was made. They do not demonstrate the promised continuation itself. The consulted museum account labels spell 25’s purpose but does not furnish a complete hieratic transcription. Its illustrative translations for other spells come from a revised Faulkner rendering of Ani and are not silently reassigned to Reri. The present case therefore rests on a dated, identified funerary practice, not a manufactured quotation.

At register 3, **Symbol answers to source** through the name’s reference to this particular deceased person. **Account does not replace source** because the surviving object is evidence of a provision for Reri, not the whole person or an empirical proof of his continuing existence. **Trust keeps the return route active** in the essay’s comparison as an entrusted act of preservation whose intended recipient exceeds present verification. The Egyptian ritual conception and the native formal-limit argument remain distinct. **Account re-enters source-field** when the preserved name and arrangement condition later remembrance and interpretation. The material survival makes a later encounter possible; it does not prove that every later reader remembered Reri, or that the original rite produced its intended afterlife result.

This case gives the field an exact asymmetry. The historical person cannot be made to answer a modern curator as a living interlocutor. Answerability instead falls upon the present account: retain the object’s identity, period, attributed purpose and limits, and let a corrected reading change what is said of the person. The record can sustain an address without owning its bearer. Preserving the name is thereby a determinate practice with a source, not evidence that Egyptian rn and an Arabic divine Name name the same kind of being or derive from one word.

The case **returns-to** [C21](../../../../section-rooms/arguments/concepts/C21-Living-Symbol-Idol.md) with a preserved sign’s office distinguished from possession of its bearer. Material survival alone decides neither living symbol nor idol. Full spell transcription and translation remain Open; the admitted object and attributed funerary provision do not depend on inventing them.

The five comparisons give the source-return different work: discriminative classification must retain its warrants; an entrusted record must remain answerable to material purpose; a political designation must sustain practicable speech; a religious enumeration must retain its act and attributed promise; a funerary name must preserve the particular person and provision it records. The Greek token, English tally and hāl/hol distinction remain independently sourced branches. These acquired relations complete the initial comparative development at their stated registers. The named primary collation, chronology, reception and empirical tasks remain Open; the comparison neither requires nor supplies a universal genealogy.

The [Bohm dossier](../../dossiers/bohm.md) **historicises** the sources of the dialogical comparison: physical interpretation, the dated 1975 conversation, an independently admitted handout and SEED’s later programme retain separate carriers. Their register-3 return asks whether a disclosed assumption and a contributor’s correction can change the next shared question while preserving the originating authority.

The [process dossier](../../dossiers/process.md) **qualifies** Account re-entry at register 3 through qualitative succession, concrescence, biological production, formal self-reference and symbolic transformation. Each return states its own changed condition. A later record is not thereby lived duration, and a self-editing instrument is not thereby an autopoietic production network.

The [process-science history](../../histories/traditions-and-disciplines/process-systems-science/DEVELOPMENT.md) **historicises** those distinct continuations through their selected editions, practices and instruments. Its chronology does not assert a single chain of influence. The achieved account returns with the object and transformation each source actually permits another inquiry to investigate.
